problem_description: When Deductive Logico was invited to a fancy dinner party at a mansion in the Hollywood Hills, he thought he had finally made it. Unfortunately, he was not the guest of honor: he was there to solve the murder of the guest of honor.

suspects.name: The Amazing Aureolin
suspects.description: A magician who perfected the sawing-your-husband-in-two routine. Then, she made his body disappear.

suspects.name: Midnight III
suspects.description: The grandson of the founder of Midnight Movies and a self-described self-made man.

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: A mystery writer whose books have sold more copies than the Bible and Shakespeare combined.

locations.name: The Enormous Bathroom
locations.description: A bathroom that is bigger than Deductive Logico's house.

locations.name: The Bedroom
locations.description: A California king-sized bed, unmade, stands in a spotless white room.

locations.name: The Screening Room
locations.description: Red velvet seats and a popcorn machine create the ultimate screening experience.

weapons.name: A Fork
weapons.description: Actually a lot more gruesome than a knife, if you think about it.

weapons.name: An Aluminum Pipe
weapons.description: Safer than lead, unless it hits you in the head.

weapons.name: A Heavy Candle
weapons.description: Heavy enough to kill, and yet it lightens the room.

clues: The Amazing Aureolin trusted the suspect who brought a fork.
Midnight III was still brandishing an aluminum pipe when Logico arrived.
A heavy candle was not found in the bedroom.
Dame Obsidian was found hiding beneath red velvet seats.
The body was found inside a marble tub.

problem_name: And Then There Was Another One
problem_description: Deductive Logico was thrilled when he heard an old man had been killed on a secluded island. Of course, that was bad, but Logico had always wanted to solve one of those secluded island murders, and this was his big chance.

suspects.name: Signor Emerald
suspects.description: An Italian jeweler of great renown, Signor Emerald has traveled the world in search of rare, precious stones, which are always falling out of his pockets.

suspects.name: Father Mango
suspects.description: He has taken a vow of poverty, but he drives a BMW. He's taken a vow of obedience, but he has a staff of twenty-five. He's taken a vow of chastity, too, which is why he's on vacation.

suspects.name: Miss Saffron
suspects.description: Gorgeous and charming, but maybe not all there in the brains department. Or maybe that's what she wants you to think. Or maybe she wants you to think that's what she wants you to think.

locations.name: The Cliffs
locations.description: A steep cliff overlooking the ocean. You could fall, but maybe the jagged rocks would break your fall.

locations.name: The Ancient Ruins
locations.description: Some old standing stones with strange glyphs carved on them.

locations.name: The Docks
locations.description: Old, rotten docks that have certainly seen better days. Look out for sharks!

weapons.name: A Bear Trap
weapons.description: If you think it's too gruesome to use on a person, just think how the bears feel!

weapons.name: An Ordinary Brick
weapons.description: Just a regular, ordinary brick. Nothing special. Just a brick.

weapons.name: A Harpoon
weapons.description: You could kill a fish with this. Or, honestly, you could kill anything with it.

clues: The suspect who brought an ordinary brick was a parishioner of Father Mango's.
Miss Saffron had a bear trap in her purse.
The suspect whose family's company produced Logico's magnifying glass was on the cliffs.
The ancient ruins seemed to hypnotize the hazel eyes of the suspect standing beside them.
By the time Logico got there, the old man's body had been nibbled on by sharks.

problem_description: Detective Logico visited an art museum, which was very confusing to him. No murder was as baffling as some of these paintings. So he was quite relieved when an experimental artist was killed in mysterious circumstances: finally, something he could understand.

suspects.name: Captain Slate
suspects.description: A real-life astronaut. The first woman to travel around the dark side of the moon, and also the first to be suspected of murdering her copilot.

suspects.name: Bishop Azure
suspects.description: A bishop in a local church, she has been known to pray for both her friends and her enemies. Of course, she asks for different things...

suspects.name: Blackstone, Esq.
suspects.description: Incredibly talented at the most important skill for an attorney: getting paid.

locations.name: The Rooftop Garden
locations.description: A rooftop garden! With pigeons! And you can feed the pigeons! Very cool.

locations.name: The Entry Hall
locations.description: With a plaque on the wall, even the architecture of the entry hall is art.

locations.name: An Art Studio
locations.description: In the back of the museum, it's littered with flyers for art classes.

weapons.name: A Glass of Poisoned Wine
weapons.description: This is your typical glass of poisoned wine. A mystery classic.

weapons.name: An Abstract Statue
weapons.description: No matter how hard he looked at this, Logico did not understand.

weapons.name: A Rare Vase
weapons.description: Logico thought about how, technically, every vase someone makes by hand is rare, because there is only one of them.

clues: Blackstone, Esq., was suspicious of the person who brought an abstract statue.
Captain Slate brought a glass of poisoned wine.
An abstract statue was not in the art studio. (Sometimes the students' art seemed abstract, but that was just because it was bad.)
Either Blackstone, Esq., was standing on top of flyers for art classes, or Captain Slate was in the rooftop garden.
The body of the experimental artist was found under a plaque on the wall.

problem_description: Once he got back to the mainland, Deductive Logico took a train. Unfortunately, somebody else took the life of the conductor. Now, the train was racing down the tracks, and nobody knew what to do except Logico: he knew he had to crack the case.

suspects.name: Vice President Mauve
suspects.description: A vice president of TekCo Futures. If she asks you to step into her metaverse, politely decline.

suspects.name: Chef Aubergine
suspects.description: It is said that she once killed her husband, cooked him, and then served him at her restaurant. It's not true, but just the fact that it's said about her tells you something.

suspects.name: Philosopher Bone
suspects.description: A dashing, dark philosopher who pioneered the ethical theory that he is not responsible for his actions, but he should be paid for them.

locations.name: The Locomotive
locations.description: The deafening sound of the steam engine prevents Deductive Logico from thinking.

locations.name: The Caboose
locations.description: The back of the train lets you see where you're leaving, and what you're leaving behind...

locations.name: The Roof
locations.description: What with the wind and the smoke from the smokestack, it's hard to get your bearings up here.

weapons.name: An Imported Italian Knife
weapons.description: It looks priceless, and that's technically true, because it's worthless.

weapons.name: Leather Luggage
weapons.description: This luggage is hideous. The leather looked way better on the cow.

weapons.name: A Rolled-Up Newspaper (With a Crowbar Inside)
weapons.description: You think, that's just a newspaper! But then... wham!

clues: A page from the classifieds was found near the heat of a steam engine.
Chef Aubergine and the person who brought leather luggage had a history together.
The tallest suspect never set foot in the caboose.
Philosopher Bone was seen wandering around outdoors.
The conductor had been stabbed to death.

problem_description: When Deductive Logico came to in a private hospital, his knew his injuries wouldn't hurt half as much as the bill. But his surgeon, Dr. Crimson, offered a trade: if he solved another patient's murder, they'd give him a two percent discount. He immediately agreed.

suspects.name: Officer Copper
suspects.description: The best part of being a policewoman criminal is that you can cut out the middleman and fail to investigate your own crimes.

suspects.name: Dr. Crimson
suspects.description: She's the smartest doctor she's ever met, according to her, and she's probably right. Yeah, she smokes, but if she gets cancer, she'll find a cure.

suspects.name: Sister Lapis
suspects.description: A nun who travels the world, doing God's work on His dime. Her habit is cashmere, and her habit is spending.

locations.name: The Parking Lot
locations.description: An enormous parking lot with uniformed valets parking luxury sedans and other vehicles.

locations.name: The Roof
locations.description: Lots and other industrial equipment cover the roof, providing a number of excellent hiding spots.

locations.name: The Gift Shop
locations.description: This hospital is so nice you can buy jewelry at the gift shop. But don't worry: there's a discount rack, too.

weapons.name: A Vial of Acid
weapons.description: According to the label, you should not take a sip of this, no matter how tempting it seems.

weapons.name: A Heavy Microscope
weapons.description: The slides are so tiny, but the microscope's so heavy!

weapons.name: A Surgical Scalpel
weapons.description: Somehow, it being smaller makes it seem more dangerous.

clues: A vial of acid was certainly not on the roof. (They had acid-detecting sensors there.)
The suspect who was in the gift shop had light brown eyes.
Officer Copper had a weapon with a label on it reading DO NOT DRINK.
Surprisingly, Dr. Crimson did not bring her surgical scalpel (or any surgical scalpel, for that matter).
The patient's body was found beneath a luxury sedan.

problem_description: While Deductive Logico was walking home, he was stopped in a dark alley by a dark figure who said that Dame Obsidian was guilty: she'd framed a semi-innocent magician (see Case 1: Murder in Hollywood). Before the dark figure could say more, he was murdered.

suspects.name: General Coffee
suspects.description: An espresso connoisseur who once sent his men to die in the jungle to harvest a single bean.

suspects.name: Cosmonaut Bluski
suspects.description: An ex-Soviet spaceman whose blood flows red. Sure, that's normal, but for him it's patriotic.

suspects.name: Midnight III
suspects.description: He argues the studio should focus on murder mysteries again to regain their former glory.

locations.name: The Metal Fence
locations.description: Your typical chain-link fence. What more do you want?

locations.name: The Dumpster
locations.description: It does not smell good. No, it does not. It smells awful, actually.

locations.name: The Distracting Graffiti
locations.description: The dragon-ril really ruins the noir vibes.

weapons.name: Piano Wire
weapons.description: Somewhere out there, there's a piano missing a wire, and it's about to ruin a concert.

weapons.name: A Crowbar
weapons.description: Honestly, they're used more often for crime than anything else.

weapons.name: A Poisonous Dart
weapons.description: One stick of this dart and you're dead.

clues: Midnight III had that familiar chain-link pattern pressed into his face.
Cosmonaut Bluski always packed for outer space: he had a light-weight weapon.
The Detective Club sent Logico a message written in Detective Code: TVMVIZO XLUUVV WRW MLG SZEV GSV XILDYZI. (See Exhibit A.)
Cosmonaut Bluski did not bring piano wire: he was tone-deaf.
Either a crowbar or a poisonous dart was by the distracting graffiti.
There was an awful smell around the body—even for a body!

problem_description: Deductive Logico traveled to Dame Obsidian's quaint little village, and immediately, Logico learned a new word: "vicar." He didn't know what it meant, but he knew how to use it in a sentence, like, "The vicar has been murdered, and I'm going to find whodunit."

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: One of her most famous books is about a mystery writer who frames an innocent magician. Suspicious!

suspects.name: Deacon Verdigris
suspects.description: A deacon in the church. She handles the parishioners' donations and, sometimes, their secrets.

suspects.name: Earl Grey
suspects.description: He comes from a long line of Earl Greys. Yes, of the tea. No, he doesn't sign autographs. But he'll give you a free bag if you ask.

locations.name: The Manor House
locations.description: The dame's. It's filled with giant portraits of many generations of dead rich white guys.

locations.name: The Chapel
locations.description: A place of vows and secrets.

locations.name: The Ancient Ruins
locations.description: These same standing stones again! Each of them has a strange labyrinth carved on its side.

weapons.name: A Bottle of Cyanide
weapons.description: It's almond-scented poison, but it can also get rid of headaches (like your husband).

weapons.name: A Pair of Gardening Shears
weapons.description: Gardening is a great hobby. But honestly, it's easier to get good tomatoes by killing for them.

weapons.name: Yarn
weapons.description: Sometimes, when you realize you've missed a stitch, you could just strangle somebody.

clues: Logico smelled almonds beneath a stained-glass window.
Dame Obsidian was not in her manor house. Or any manor house, for that matter.
Yes, he owned a tea empire, but Earl Grey never gardened, and he wouldn't be caught dead holding a pair of shears.
Deacon Verdigris was visiting the ancient ruins to research an article he was writing about the local pagan practices prior to the arrival of the church.
The vicar was strangled—most embarrassingly with yarn.

problem_description: Immediately after the last one, there was another murder in Dame Obsidian's house! That made her look even guiltier, Logico thought. Especially since it was her butler who was murdered. What kind of person kills somebody else's butler?

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: As additional background: a week after Dame Obsidian's second husband disappeared, she paved over her garden. The papers had a field day with that. But her sales doubled.

suspects.name: Sir Rulean
suspects.description: A sophisticated gentleman who was just recently knighted, if you believe the shoddy paperwork he carries with him.

suspects.name: Miss Saffron
suspects.description: Gorgeous and stunning, but maybe not all there in the brains department. Or maybe that's what she wants you to think. Or maybe she wants you to think that's what she wants you to think.

locations.name: The Spooky Attic
locations.description: Nothing but cobwebs, family heirlooms, and secrets.

locations.name: The Master Bedroom
locations.description: The bed is so big that the bedroom had to be built around it.

locations.name: The Grounds
locations.description: A meticulously maintained, solid green two-inch monoculture.

weapons.name: A Magnifying Glass
weapons.description: You could use this to find a clue, read the fine print, or start a small fire.

weapons.name: An Antique Clock
weapons.description: Tick, tock, tick, tock. Technically, time is killing us all slowly.

weapons.name: An Axe
weapons.description: This axe could chop a tree down. Or a person down!

clues: Either Miss Saffron brought an axe or an axe was in the master bedroom.
Sir Rulean had been hiding from the person who brought an axe.
An antique clock was certainly not on the grounds: it was an inside clock.
Miss Saffron was seen using a weapon to read the fine print in the ads of a gossip magazine.
Blood was splattered on a family heirloom.

problem_name: Hedge Your Bets, The Constable Cried
problem_description: While Logico was wondering if it were possible Dame Obsidian was actually innocent, he heard a scream from her hedge maze. He ran into it, got lost, figured it out, and then found Dame Obsidian, who he was now certain was innocent, on account of she was dead.

suspects.name: Constable Copper
suspects.description: The identical twin of Officer Copper. When their parents divorced, she moved across the ocean. But they have so much in common. Same height, same job, same propensity to violence.

suspects.name: Lord Lavender
suspects.description: A politically conservative MP in the House of Lords, as well as the musical theater composer behind such hits as Dogs and Mr. Moses Megastar.

suspects.name: Miss Saffron
suspects.description: Gorgeous and stunning, but maybe not all there in the brains department. Or maybe that's what she wants you to think. Or maybe she wants you to think that's what she wants you to think.

locations.name: The Fountain
locations.description: A fountain at the center of the maze, if you can find it.

locations.name: The Lookout Tower
locations.description: From above the garden, you can see everything. Plus, there's a map on the wall that reveals (some of) the maze's secrets.

locations.name: The Ancient Ruins
locations.description: These same old ruins again! They were here long before the rest of the maze.

weapons.name: A Pair of Gardening Shears
weapons.description: They're getting a little rusty, and they might leave screws behind.

weapons.name: A Flowerpot
weapons.description: If you use this to murder, please re-pot the flowers first.

weapons.name: Poisoned Tea
weapons.description: Enjoy a nice sip of tea, followed by a long, long nap.

clues: Poisoned tea was certainly not in the ancient ruins, nor was it in the fountain.
The tallest suspect and the person who brought a pair of gardening shears had a history together.
A flowerpot was not in the ancient ruins. Or was it? (It wasn't.)
Miss Saffron was addicted to a product made by a friend, Earl Grey, and she added just a little poison.
Dame Obsidian's body was found beside a blood-splattered map.

problem_name: Eat, Drink, and Be Merry, For a Jerk Just Died
problem_description: Because of a mistake he made with time zones (the hardest problem in all of deductive analysis), Logico missed his flight home. So he went to the village pub, where everyone was celebrating the death of a loud-mouthed jerk. They all wanted to know whodunit (so they could buy him drinks), and Logico was happy to oblige.

suspects.name: Brother Brownstone
suspects.description: A monk who has dedicated his life to the church, specifically to making money for it.

suspects.name: Comrade Champagne
suspects.description: A communist and a rich one. Comrade Champagne likes nothing more than to travel the world, sharing the message of communism with his fellow vacationers.

suspects.name: Grandmaster Rose
suspects.description: A chess grand master who is always plotting his next move. Like how to bump off his next opponent! (1. e4)

locations.name: The Center Bar
locations.description: They're giving out free drinks to celebrate the jerk being dead.

locations.name: The Corner Booth
locations.description: Shrouded in shadow, you sit at this booth if you don't want to be seen.

locations.name: The Cramped Bathroom
locations.description: So small it seems like it was designed for a discount airplane.

weapons.name: A Corkscrew
weapons.description: Once Logico started looking, he saw weapons everywhere.

weapons.name: A Bottle of Wine
weapons.description: Watch out for stains, because the red doesn't come out.

weapons.name: A Crystal Ball
weapons.description: If you look into it, it will tell you your future, so long as your future is a crystal ball.

clues: A red stain was found in a teeny, tiny space.
The chess player was suspicious of the person who brought a bottle of wine.
A corkscrew was certainly not in the center bar.
The suspect with the corkscrew had blond hair.
They were giving out free drinks right over the jerk's still-warm body!

problem_name: The Case of the Coffee Shop Killer
problem_description: Once Deductive Logico was back home, he went to his favorite coffee shop in order to ponder what had happened to Dame Obsidian. While he was lost in thought, a barista lost her life. He couldn't save her, but he could solve her murder.

suspects.name: General Coffee
suspects.description: An espresso connoisseur who likes his coffee like he likes his war: always.

suspects.name: Coach Raspberry
suspects.description: One of the best coaches this side of the Mississippi, regardless of which side you happen to be on. Some people say he has a gambling problem, but he just says he loves danger.

suspects.name: Bookie-Winner Gainsboro
suspects.description: He won the Bookington Award for his novel, which he will tell you within two minutes of meeting you. The book is six thousand pages long, and it's about dirt.

locations.name: The Courtyard
locations.description: Sun-dappled tables and chairs sit beneath a magnificent oak, perfect for conversation... or murder.

locations.name: The Bean Room
locations.description: Full of bags and bags of beans. The smell is so strong and delicious that Logico wants to eat the beans.

locations.name: The Counter
locations.description: There is a little bell that alerts the baristas you are here so they can start ignoring you.

weapons.name: An Ordinary Brick
weapons.description: Just a regular, ordinary brick. Nothing special. Just a brick.

weapons.name: A Metal Straw
weapons.description: Better for the planet than a plastic straw, but more deadly!

weapons.name: A Poisoned Cup of Coffee
weapons.description: It's poisoned with ricin, which is made from castor beans. So technically this is a two-bean soup.

clues: Bookie-Winner Gainsboro had never been in the courtyard, and he never wanted to go, if you asked him.
Coach Raspberry used to run plays with the person who brought a poisoned cup of coffee.
Logico found a regular brick chip buried beneath bags of beans.
The person who was at the counter was the former owner of Deductive Logico's coffee cup. (See Exhibit A.)
A metal straw was used to commit the murder.

problem_description: Detective Logico decided to investigate the mystery of Dame Obsidian by investigating the mysteries of Dame Obsidian, so he went to a local mystery bookshop. But the first mystery he found was the death of the bookshop proprietor.

suspects.name: Captain Slate
suspects.description: A real-life astronaut. The first woman to travel around the dark side of the moon, and also the first to be suspected of murdering her copilot.

suspects.name: Comrade Champagne
suspects.description: A communist and a rich one. Comrade Champagne likes nothing more than to travel the world, sharing the message of communism with his fellow vacationers.

suspects.name: Director Dusty
suspects.description: A true filmmaker. The only thing he cares about is getting his movie made. No matter what.

locations.name: The Discount Rack
locations.description: You can find a lot of great books here, and soon, a half-solved copy of Murdle.

locations.name: The Front Counter
locations.description: Where you can actually buy the books, or any of the little trinkets they have for sale.

locations.name: The Rare Books Room
locations.description: A single Dame Obsidian first edition costs more than Logico's father made in his lifetime.

weapons.name: A Tote Bag
weapons.description: Bibliophile mafiosos use these canvas bags for hits. You can also carry books in them.

weapons.name: A Bone Folder
weapons.description: Yeah, it's made from an animal bone, but just because you've killed before doesn't mean you'll kill again.

weapons.name: A Paperback
weapons.description: Too light to hit someone over the head, but the ink is so cheap it's toxic.

clues: A tote bag was not found in the discount rack.
A smudge of toxic ink was found by the front counter.
An anti-shoplifting mirror caught the reflection of the eyes of the person in the rare books room: they were dark brown.
There weren't any film books in the discount rack, so Director Dusty wasn't there.
A chip of animal bone was found inside the body of the proprietor.

problem_description: Dame Obsidian had written mysteries in many different places and periods, and Logico was determined to read them all. The first was a Western, filled with red herrings, black hats, and a twist worthy of a lasso. A rancher had been killed, and it looked like the suspects were based on real people.

suspects.name: Cowboy Raspberry
suspects.description: One of the best cowboys this side of the Mississippi, regardless of which side you happen to be on. Some people say he has a rustlin' problem, but he just says he loves danger.

suspects.name: Justice Pine
suspects.description: Master of the rural courthouse and possessed of a firm belief in her own form of frontier justice.

suspects.name: Corporal Coffee
suspects.description: Back in those days, if you liked coffee, you liked it black. And the corporal liked coffee.

locations.name: The Saloon
locations.description: The worst saloon that anybody who ever visited had ever visited.

locations.name: The Watering Hole
locations.description: You can get the cleanest water in the West here. It's dark brown.

locations.name: The "Hotel"
locations.description: A "hotel" that provides certain "amenities" including "charging" by the "hour."

weapons.name: A Stabbin' Knife
weapons.description: Just the kinda knife that's perfect for stabbin'.

weapons.name: A Cactus
weapons.description: Watch out for the needles—and also for someone hitting you with it.

weapons.name: Tainted Moonshine
weapons.description: This'll kill you, that's for sure. Even the smell is dangerous.

clues: Some needles were found soaking in dark brown water.
Justice Pine was suspicious of the person who brought a stabbin' knife. (Reasonable.)
Corporal Coffee had never been in the "hotel."
Whoever had the cactus had blue eyes.
Tainted moonshine was used to murder the rancher.

problem_description: Next, Logico read a book set in Victorian London—the capital of the whodunit! It was obviously based on heavy research, but the dame played all the hits: bloody letters, a shoe print in the snow, and the murder of the richest man in town, thousandaire Lord Lavender.

suspects.name: Baron Maroon
suspects.description: An incredibly haughty man who holds a grudge. Nobody wants to offend the baron. At least, nobody who's still alive...

suspects.name: Earl Grey
suspects.description: He comes from a shorter (but still long) line of Earl Greys. And this Earl Grey does sign autographs, but he charges for the tea bags.

suspects.name: Viscount Eminence
suspects.description: The oldest man you have ever seen. It is said that he outlived all of his sons and was born before his father.

locations.name: The Investigation Institute
locations.description: A recently founded organization that investigates spiritualism and other related phenomena.

locations.name: A Potentially Haunted Mansion
locations.description: People keep seeing ghosts here, especially around the furnace in the basement.

locations.name: A Coffee House
locations.description: Where you can drink coffee and discuss the latest ghastly happenings.

weapons.name: A Knife
weapons.description: Not a famous knife. Just a regular one. Maybe it'll be famous soon, though!

weapons.name: The Plague
weapons.description: Well, not the plague, but one of them that's been going around.

weapons.name: A Jeweled Scepter
weapons.description: Part of the crown jewels, and like most of them, it was stolen from another country.

clues: A knife was found in the headquarters of a recently founded organization.
Viscount Eminence hated ghosts, so he had not been anywhere near the potentially haunted mansion.
Baron Maroon's love affair with the person who brought the plague was the biggest subplot.
Fingerprints on the jeweled scepter proved it was held by a left-handed suspect.
Lord Lavender's body was found next to a shattered cup of coffee.

problem_name: The Perplexing Problem of the Parrot
problem_description: Arrr! The next Obsidian novel was set in the world of piracy, and it was full of thrills, chills, and multicolored beards. Logico was enthralled by the twist in the first act, when Blackbeard's parrot was murdered. Oh man, Logico thought, whoever crossed Blackbeard is in trouble!

suspects.name: Blackbeard
suspects.description: Famous, feared, respected for the beard.

suspects.name: Bluebeard
suspects.description: Actually a French wife-murderer, and not a pirate at all.

suspects.name: Nobeard
suspects.description: His name used to be Redbeard, but then he shaved. A part-time pirate.

locations.name: The Great Whirlpool
locations.description: Apparently there's a big hole in the ocean and all the water's draining out.

locations.name: The Pirate Cove
locations.description: Where all the pirates go to drink and plan where to bury their treasure. (Maybe by those ancient ruins...)

locations.name: The Pirate Ship
locations.description: Yo ho ho, a pirate's life for me—and death.

weapons.name: A Cannon
weapons.description: Usually used to kill more than one person (or parrot), but exceptions can be made.

weapons.name: A Scimitar
weapons.description: Technically, it's just a bent sword, but if you call it a scimitar, it sounds cool.

weapons.name: A Fake Treasure Map
weapons.description: This map leads someone straight into a booby-trapped pit.

clues: Either Bluebeard brought a scimitar or a fake treasure map was in the pirate ship.
The second tallest suspect was seen in the place where a pirate lives and dies.
The fake treasure map was spinning around in giant circles out in the ocean, dissolving in the saltwater.
The shortest suspect was suspicious of the person with the cannon.
The parrot was found floating in the waters of the pirate cove.

problem_description: Deductive Logico went to Dame Obsidian's literary agency to look for a body. He found one, but it wasn't Dame Obsidian's. It was the body of a powerful agent, dead in his office.

suspects.name: Editor Ivory
suspects.description: The greatest romance editor of all time. She invented the enemies-to-lovers genre, and she was the first person to put a naked man on the cover of a book.

suspects.name: Assistant Applegreen
suspects.description: Her father is a principal, and she is making him proud. But you know what she's not making? Enough money.

suspects.name: Agent Ink
suspects.description: An agent with a heart of gold, but a mind for gold, too. If you like living, don't cross her.

locations.name: The Balcony
locations.description: Standing on the balcony, you can look out over the city you run.

locations.name: The Best Office
locations.description: The best-earning agent of the month gets this office. The worst is fired.

locations.name: The Unsolicited Submissions Room
locations.description: A room that doubles as an incinerator.

weapons.name: An Antique Typewriter
weapons.description: You can write your themes subtly, or you can hit them over the head with it.

weapons.name: A Giant Stack of Books
weapons.description: You can shove this over and crush someone beneath it. But it's hard to carry around.

weapons.name: A Ream of Paper
weapons.description: You could use these blank pages to give someone a thousand paper cuts or one paper bash.

clues: Editor Ivory and the person who brought a giant stack of books had known each other for years.
Assistant Applegreen wasn't allowed to go out on the balcony.
Logico received a clue from the Detective Club, written in their signature code: ZTVMG RMP SZW Z NVWRFN-DVRTSG DVZKLM. (See Exhibit A.)
Whoever was in the unsolicited submissions room had to be right-handed, because otherwise you get burned.
The agent who died in his office had been the best-earning agent that month.

problem_name: The Case of the Contract & The Captain
problem_description: On the yacht of legendary book publisher Chairman Chalk, Logico signed a contract for a book series and got to work solving the murder of a sailor, which he got to add to the book. Or, at least, he would, as soon as he cracked it.

suspects.name: Bookie-Winner Gainsboro
suspects.description: He won the Bookington Award for his novel, which he will tell you within two minutes of meeting you. The book is six thousand pages long, and it's about dirt.

suspects.name: Chairman Chalk
suspects.description: He figured out the publishing business years ago and never looked back. He called ebooks a "fad" and still owns a rotary phone. He is worth a billion dollars.

suspects.name: Agent Ink
suspects.description: An agent with a heart of gold, but a mind for gold, too. If you like living, don't cross her.

locations.name: The Deck
locations.description: Look out over the ocean, but not too far or someone might push you.

locations.name: The Engine Room
locations.description: This is a green yacht: it's powered by a nuclear reactor. When the uranium rods are spent, just toss them into the ocean.

locations.name: The Dining Hall
locations.description: They've hired an award-winning chef for cheap because he's banned from working on land.

weapons.name: An Antique Anchor
weapons.description: It's covered in moss and the chain is rusty: it looks awesome.

weapons.name: A Golden Pen
weapons.description: For signing contracts and stabbing competitors. Even the ink is gold.

weapons.name: A Baby Shark
weapons.description: Just throw and go: toss it at your enemies and watch those baby teeth go.

clues: The second tallest suspect had never been in the engine room.
Someone suffering from obvious seasickness wrote out this scrambled clue: WEEOHRV ASW NO HTE CDEK WSA TEFL HEDNAD.
Bookie-Winner Gainsboro was jealous of the person with the golden pen. Why didn't I bring a golden pen? he wondered.
The yacht had a strict no anchors in the dining hall policy, and nobody would have violated it, even to commit a murder.
Chairman Chalk didn't bring an antique anchor.
A tiny, sharp tooth was biting into the sailor's body.

problem_description: Last year, at the 138th annual Bookington Awards, Deductive Logico was nominated for one of the most prestigious awards: Best Debut Murder Mystery Puzzle Book Based on a True Story. Unfortunately, right after the winner was announced, the president of the Bookington Society was killed. But whodunit? And who won the Bookie?

suspects.name: Philosopher Bone
suspects.description: A dashing, dark philosopher who pioneered the ethical theory that he is not responsible for his actions, but he should be paid for them.

suspects.name: Deductive Logico
suspects.description: He was finally there for the actual murder, which means he's a suspect.

suspects.name: Silverton the Legend
suspects.description: An acclaimed actor of the Golden Age, now in his golden years.

locations.name: The Stage
locations.description: Where you accept your award at the lectern to the deafening applause of dozens of clapping hands.

locations.name: A Nominee Table
locations.description: Where the nominees are seated together (for the sake of drama).

locations.name: Backstage
locations.description: Interns and assistants struggle with the ropes, levers, and control boards.

weapons.name: A Bookie
weapons.description: The diminutive nickname of the most prestigious award in publishing. The fake gold is flaking off.

weapons.name: A Heavy Book
weapons.description: Gainsboro's six-thousand-page dirt book.

weapons.name: A Fountain Pen
weapons.description: With this, you can sign checks or stab necks. Unfortunately, it leaks ink.

clues: Philosopher Bone hated the person who won the Bookie.
A frantic fan gave Deductive Logico a piece of paper she had scrawled a scrambled clue on: NTVIROLSE ETH NGDELE ASW CIPUSISSUO OF HET PENSRO HWO HBTROGU A VHYEA KOBO.
Whoever sat at the nominee table had a medium-weight weapon.
Either Silverton the Legend brought a heavy book, or Silverton the Legend was behind a lectern.
The victim's body was found slumped over a control board.

problem_description: Deductive Logico's publisher asked him to go on a book tour to promote Murdle, but they had to cancel one of the stops because a bookstore owner had been murdered by one of their other authors. But due to ethics in publishing, they couldn't say which stop was canceled. He had to figure it out himself.

suspects.name: Chancellor Tuscany
suspects.description: As the head of Deduction College, she has deduced the best ways to get away with murder. Only in theory, of course!

suspects.name: Secretary Celadon
suspects.description: The secretary of defense, and someone who is personally responsible for a number of war crimes, some of which are now named after her.

suspects.name: Vice President Mauve
suspects.description: A vice president of TekCo Futures. If she asks you to step into her metaverse, firmly refuse.

locations.name: Hollywood
locations.description: Tinseltown, the City of Angels, La La Land, the Dream Factory.

locations.name: Tektopia
locations.description: He built a fully automated city in the desert. His goal is to disrupt food. He will succeed.

locations.name: The Republic of Drakonia
locations.description: Previously the Holy Republic of Drakonia, now the Free Republic of Drakonia.

weapons.name: A Laptop
weapons.description: The machine you work on. It's also connected to every distraction ever made.

weapons.name: A Poisoned Candle
weapons.description: If you light this candle, everyone in the room will die. But it has a nice lavender scent.

weapons.name: A Sextant
weapons.description: Get your head out of the gutter and start thinking like a sailor.

clues: Everyone in the Dream Factory has a laptop.
No sextant was in the Republic of Drakonia—that's right, not one in the whole country.
Secretary Celadon refused to visit Hollywood until their movies treated the military better.
The sextant was held by someone whose last name began with one of the letters in Deductive Logico's Detective Club member number. (See Exhibit A.)
The dead body smelled like lavender.

problem_description: Once the book tour was over, Deductive Logico stumbled back to his office. It was small, but it seemed bigger than it was because of how orderly he kept it. Unfortunately for Logico, four things were disrupting his organizational system: the three people waiting on him, and the dead body between them.

suspects.name: Cosmonaut Bluski
suspects.description: An ex-Soviet spaceman whose blood flows red. Sure, that's normal, but for him it's patriotic.

suspects.name: Dr. Crimson
suspects.description: She's the smartest doctor she's ever met, according to her, and she's probably right. Yeah, she skydives, but if something goes wrong, she'll calculate just how to fall.

suspects.name: General Coffee
suspects.description: An espresso connoisseur who once made a pot of coffee so strong that it killed a man.

locations.name: The Main Office
locations.description: A desk, shelves of logic books, and a window with a view of a brick wall.

locations.name: The Closet
locations.description: Where jackets are carefully sorted from A to Z.

locations.name: The Waiting Room
locations.description: Logico doesn't have a receptionist so there's just a bell and a sign that says PLEASE WAIT.

weapons.name: A Deduction College Diploma
weapons.description: With its heavy oak frame, you could really do some damage. And they say a logic degree is useless.

weapons.name: Leather Gloves
weapons.description: Beware someone who wears leather gloves. They've already killed a cow: who's next?

weapons.name: A Magnifying Glass
weapons.description: You could use this to find a clue, read the fine print, or start a small fire.

clues: Cosmonaut Bluski hated the person who brought a magnifying glass.
A magnifying glass was discovered near a window view of a brick wall.
Dr. Crimson was seen behind alphabetically ordered jackets.
Leather gloves were certainly not in the waiting room.
A logic degree was used to commit the murder.

problem_description: Deductive Logico followed the old pirate map: it led him to an oil field at the edge of an ocean. When he arrived at the X, he saw Dame Obsidian was already there, as were two other people, or three, if you counted the body.

suspects.name: Chairman Chalk
suspects.description: He figured out the publishing business years ago and never looked back. He called ebooks a "fad" and still owns a rotary phone. He is worth a billion dollars.

suspects.name: Midnight III
suspects.description: Maybe the only person capable of returning Midnight Movies to its former glory.

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: Back from the dead! But Logico remembered when an interviewer asked her how she got all of her ideas for all of her fictional perfect murders, and she chuckled for two full minutes.

locations.name: An Oil Derrick
locations.description: They're digging another well right now with this massive derrick.

locations.name: The Offices
locations.description: Such a low temperature that it uses most of the energy the field produces.

locations.name: The Ancient Ruins
locations.description: You can see them from the edge of the fields, silhouetted in the light of the setting sun.

weapons.name: A Crowbar
weapons.description: Honestly, at this point, they're used more often for crime than anything else.

weapons.name: A Piece of Rebar
weapons.description: A long piece of metal. If this isn't a weapon, nothing is. Often used with powdered cement.

weapons.name: An Oil Drum
weapons.description: Really more of a giant can than a drum: you've never seen a band feature one of these.

clues: Nobody ever put an oil drum anywhere near the ancient ruins. It was a superstition.
Either Chairman Chalk brought an oil drum, or a crowbar was in an oil derrick.
A trusted confidant gave Deductive Logico a piece of paper with a message written in what he called the Next Letter Code: SGD RGN-QSDRS RTRODBS VZR MNS AX SGD ZMBHDMS QTHMR.
Neither Midnight III nor Dame Obsidian had ever been in the offices.
Some powdered cement was found on the victim.

problem_description: Dame Obsidian contracted the most expensive law firm in the world—Blackstone & Blackstone—and one of them (Blackstone) required Logico to come to his office to be deposed. Unfortunately, when he got there, Blackstone was indisposed (AKA dead).

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: Dame Obsidian had an army of attorneys. That's where she got the idea for her book The Army of Attorneys I Have.

suspects.name: Vice President Mauve
suspects.description: A vice president of TekCo Futures. If she asks you to step into her metaverse, walk away quickly.

suspects.name: Blackstone, Esq.
suspects.description: The other one. Incredibly talented at the most important skill for an attorney: getting paid.

locations.name: The Lobby
locations.description: It has an enormous fountain, a marble desk, and a receptionist ready to call the police.

locations.name: An Associate's Office
locations.description: Tiny, cramped, cluttered, possibly a closet. Occupied by someone who works for too little.

locations.name: A Partner's Office
locations.description: Featuring pictures of the partner with every living US president, even the really bad ones.

weapons.name: A Marble Bust
weapons.description: It's a bust of a famous lawyer, but don't look him up—you won't like what you find.

weapons.name: Confusing Contracts
weapons.description: Legalese so impenetrable it could give you an aneurysm.

weapons.name: Poisoned Inkwell
weapons.description: How was he poisoned? Well.

clues: Lawyers often use the Next Letter Code to make notes to themselves. Logico found one of them: SGD RTRODBS HM SGD ZRRNBHZSD'R NEEHBD GZC FQDDM DXDR.
The suspect with a metaverse had never been in the partner's office.
The tallest suspect had a crush on the person who brought a poisoned inkwell.
Whoever had the confusing contracts was left-handed.
A bust of a... controversial figure was found beside the victim.

problem_description: It was finally the day of Dame Obsidian's trial, and Logico wore his finest raincoat to the courthouse. He hoped to see justice done. But instead of justice, he witnessed a murder. Was the death of this clerk connected to Dame Obsidian? Or just another everyday killing?

suspects.name: Coach Raspberry
suspects.description: One of the best coaches this side of the Mississippi, regardless of which side you're on.

suspects.name: Officer Copper
suspects.description: Ever since she murdered that guy, Officer Copper has been on administrative leave, which is when they leave the administrative work to her.

suspects.name: Father Mango
suspects.description: He has taken a vow of poverty, but he drives a BMW. He's taken a vow of obedience, but he has a staff of twenty-five. He's taken a vow of chastity, too, which is why he's on vacation.

locations.name: The Actual Courtroom
locations.description: Here is where Dame Obsidian's trial is going to be.

locations.name: The Parking Lot
locations.description: More cop cars than Logico has seen since he got stuck behind that police parade.

locations.name: The Judge's Chambers
locations.description: A nice desk, a good view out the window, and a closet filled with black robes.

weapons.name: A Notary Stamp
weapons.description: Stamp a classic notary stamp on anything from papers to foreheads.

weapons.name: The Scales of Justice
weapons.description: Justice may be blind, but only because someone knocked her out with these scales.

weapons.name: A Huge Pile of Paperwork
weapons.description: A riddle: one piece of paper is too light to kill. But a big enough stack can. So, which single page turns it into a weapon?

clues: Someone with a shaky hand gave Logico a message: HET SUTSPEC IN EHT UCALTA ROOOTCUMR WAS HRIGT NDDAHE.
The scales of justice were certainly not in the parking lot: that's where the cars go.
Since Officer Copper committed murder, they had her doing notary work.
Father Mango brought a huge pile of paperwork.
The body was found in the judge's chambers.

problem_description: Finally, it was time for the trial of the century, and Dame Obsidian put on a wonderful performance. But just when the jury was about to deliberate, the foreman was killed. Obviously, everyone thought Dame Obsidian did it. Did she?

suspects.name: Judge Pine
suspects.description: Master of the courtroom and possessed of a firm belief in justice, as decided by her alone.

suspects.name: Officer Copper
suspects.description: The best part of being a policewoman criminal is that you can cut out the middleman and fail to investigate your own crimes.

suspects.name: Dame Obsidian
suspects.description: Dame Obsidian looked very dignified all throughout the trial, and her book sales skyrocketed.

locations.name: The Gallery
locations.description: Where all the family members sit beside the true-crime podcast enthusiasts.

locations.name: The Judge's Bench
locations.description: You know the judge is in charge because she has the highest seat.

locations.name: The Jury Box
locations.description: In a sense, the trial was a show performed for an audience of twelve.

weapons.name: A Baton
weapons.description: A great tool for brutalizing innocent people.

weapons.name: A Gavel
weapons.description: Let's be frank: there's a reason they give the judge a big hammer. (Intimidation.)

weapons.name: A Flag
weapons.description: Flags have a long and respectable history of being used for violence.

clues: A gavel was nowhere near the true-crime enthusiasts.
Deductive Logico received a message from the Detective Club written in Detective Code: QFWTV KRMV DZH HRGGRMT LM SVI YVMXS. (See Exhibit A.)
Dame Obsidian had snuck in a baton "for self-defense," a dubious reason.
Either Officer Copper brought a gavel, or Judge Pine was in the gallery.
Like many times before, a flag was used to commit this murder.

problem_description: Almost immediately after Dame Obsidian had been incarcerated, Logico got a call from the luxurious white-collar jail to which she had been sentenced, and he learned that she had been murdered herself. Was that justice? Was it fate? All he knew was it was a mystery.

suspects.name: Secretary Celadon
suspects.description: The secretary of defense, and someone who is personally responsible for a number of international incidents, some of which are now named after her.

suspects.name: The Amazing Aureolin
suspects.description: She blames Dame Obsidian for her incarceration, which makes sense, since Dame Obsidian framed her.

suspects.name: Miss Saffron
suspects.description: Miss Saffron also blames Dame Obsidian, though it's a little less sympathetic coming from her because she was actually guilty.

locations.name: The Spa
locations.description: Built with money from the PTA (Prisoner Treats Association), although tax dollars do pay for maintenance.

locations.name: The Parking Lot
locations.description: Prisoners can pay to park their luxury vehicles here for the duration of their stay.

locations.name: A Private Suite
locations.description: If you have enough money, you can upgrade to a private suite with a big-screen TV, hot tub, and open bar.

weapons.name: A Quarter-Million-Dollar Lawyer
weapons.description: The most dangerous weapon of all. (And the most expensive.)

weapons.name: A Rope Made of Designer Clothes
weapons.description: When you need a rope but all you have are designer clothes.

weapons.name: A Pair of Golden Handcuffs
weapons.description: This is taking the metaphor too far, all right?

clues: Somebody passed Logico a slip of paper, on which a jumbled message was written: EW LLA SWA TEH ALWREY ROODISN.
Secretary Celadon had a pair of custom-made golden handcuffs.
The Detective Club sent Logico a card in Detective Code that read: GSV HSLIGVHG HFHKVXG DZH IVOZCRMT RM GSV HKZ WFIRMT GSV NFIWVI. (See Exhibit A.)
The Amazing Aureolin could not afford the private suite on her magician's salary.
Dame Obsidian was found with a rope of designer clothes around her neck.

ground_truth.what: A Rope Made of Designer Clothes

problem_name: The Murder of a Mailman QQ
problem_description: Deductive Logico went to check his PO box, but instead of finding a royalty check for Murdle, he found that a mailman had been killed, and the whole place was closed. Neither rain nor shine, thought Logico, but they close at the first sign of murder...

suspects.name: Dr. Crimson
suspects.description: She's the smartest doctor she's ever met, according to her, and she's probably right. Yeah, her diet is horrible, but if she has a heart attack, she'll operate on herself.

suspects.name: Mayor Honey
suspects.description: He knows where the bodies are buried, and he makes sure they always vote for him.

suspects.name: General Coffee
suspects.description: An espresso connoisseur who prefers the smell of coffee to napalm in the morning.

locations.name: A Mail Truck
locations.description: Practically indestructible, so it's great for joyrides, so long as you're not the one paying for gas.

locations.name: The Long Line
locations.description: People waiting to mail their letters.

locations.name: The Sorting Room
locations.description: Where the postal workers sort the junk mail, bills, and catalogs using a great machine.

weapons.name: A Letter Opener
weapons.description: A sharp knife used by people who won't just rip their letters open.

weapons.name: A Stamp Stamp
weapons.description: A stamp for stamping over stamps.

weapons.name: A Heavy Package
weapons.description: With a nice red ribbon that'll conceal blood stains.

clues: Letter openers were not allowed in the sorting room, ever since "the Incident," and that rule was not broken today.
The suspect with the heavy package was self-conscious about their baldness and would prefer it not be mentioned in clues.

statements.statement: I brought a stamp stamp.
Dr. Crimson was not in a mail truck.
A letter opener was in a mail truck.

problem_name: A Mysterious Murder in the Mysterious Woods
problem_description: Driving through the mysterious woods gave Detective Logico the chills, but maybe that was because his AC was on full blast. Pretty soon, he had to pull over, partially to solve the murder of a hitchhiker, and partially because his car died.

suspects.name: Coach Raspberry
suspects.description: One of the best coaches this side of the Mississippi, regardless of which side you're on.

suspects.name: Officer Copper
suspects.description: The best part of being a policewoman criminal is that you can cut out the middleman and fail to investigate your own crimes.

suspects.name: Grandmaster Rose
suspects.description: A chess grand master who is always plotting his next move. Like how to bump off his next opponent! (1 ... e5)

locations.name: The Skull Rock
locations.description: A rock that looks like a skull. Is it natural, or did someone carve it?

locations.name: The Ancient Ruins
locations.description: Wherever the somebody is getting murdered nearby.

locations.name: The Only Road
locations.description: A twisting, winding, half-paved road through the woods.

weapons.name: A Shovel
weapons.description: A multi-use tool: kill someone and bury them with the same shovel!

weapons.name: A Ritual Dagger
weapons.description: It's made out of some ancient metal that Logico can't identify.

weapons.name: A Poisonous Spider
weapons.description: Its unusual webbing shows it's not native to these woods.

clues: Logico caught a glimpse of the suspect with the shovel, but all he could see was that his eyes weren't blue.
A poisonous spider was not on the only road.

statements.statement: You must study the moves of the pieces. For example, Officer Copper was at the skull rock!
Well, by golly, a shovel was at the ancient ruins.
My statement? I brought a poisonous spider.

problem_name: Oh No, Not in the Chateau! QQ
problem_description: "Hello!" Logico called. "I'm here to meet with the president!" Nobody answered, and he looked around. It seemed like the chateau was designed by Escher, too. Stairways and hallways twisted around each other, and every available surface was covered in books. Perhaps the least unexpected sight was the dead body.

suspects.name: Sociologist Umber
suspects.description: As a representative from the hard sciences, she is always asking people to question their priors and if they've read Weber.

suspects.name: Philologist Flint
suspects.description: You can learn a lot about a word from its etymology, like where it came from, and what it used to mean.

suspects.name: Numerologist Night
suspects.description: A mathematical and esoteric prodigy. Not only do they know the value of X, they know the meaning of X.

locations.name: The Front Driveway
locations.description: Huge stone statues overlook the chateau.

locations.name: The Arcane Attic
locations.description: Rumored to be haunted, guaranteed to contain a bunch of old junk.

locations.name: The Ballroom
locations.description: For grand parties and also basketball games.

weapons.name: A Cursed Dagger
weapons.description: A dying duchess cursed this dagger when she used it to end her own life.

weapons.name: A Selenite Wand
weapons.description: For casting spells and bashing skulls.

weapons.name: An Exclusive Pin
weapons.description: If this is pinned to someone's lapel, they're a member of a secret society.

clues: An Aquarius was standing beside a basketball goal.
Numerologist Night calculated that the selenite wand corresponded to an inauspicious number, so they wouldn't touch it.

statements.statement: All I can say is I brought a cursed dagger.
If you consider the origin of the words, you could say: I was wearing an exclusive pin.
Based on the numbers, an exclusive pin was in the arcane attic.

problem_description: Arriving at the Investigation Institute grounds, Deductive Logico was shocked by their budget. Their grounds had a hedge maze, an observatory, even a miniature golf course! This place could have hired half the detectives in the world. Why him? And who killed the groundskeeper?

suspects.name: Cryptozoologist Cloud
suspects.description: He knows every sighting of Bigfoot, Yeti, Sasquatch, and also what the difference is.

suspects.name: Herbalist Onyx
suspects.description: In her greenhouse, she's grown every kind of plant required in the culinary, magick, and poisoning arts.

suspects.name: Chef Aubergine
suspects.description: It is said that she once killed her husband, cooked him, and then served him at her restaurant. It's not true, but just the fact that it's said about her tells you something.

locations.name: An Impossible Hedge Maze
locations.description: This was designed by a master gardener, so good luck getting out.

locations.name: The Observatory
locations.description: For studying the stars, or having a romantic evening, or committing a murder.

locations.name: The Miniature Golf Course
locations.description: Eighteen holes, featuring windmills, caves, and loop-de-loops. The works!

weapons.name: A Quasi-Perpetual Motion Machine
weapons.description: It doesn't run forever. More like two or three minutes.

weapons.name: A Dowsing Rod
weapons.description: You can find water, oil, and suckers with this.

weapons.name: Hyper-Allergenic Oil
weapons.description: You read that right. Everyone is deadly allergic to this.

clues: The second tallest suspect brought hyperallergenic oil.
It turns out that a Libra was at the seventeenth hole when the murder was committed.

statements.statement: A dowsing rod was not in a hedge maze.
A quasi-perpetual motion machine was not in the observatory.
Herbalist Onyx brought a quasi-perpetual motion machine.

problem_name: The Case of the Definitely Dead President
problem_description: Deductive Logico went to the president's office and said, "I'm here to meet with the president." Unfortunately, they said, "The president's dead." But nobody had left the room. So instead of meeting with the president, he worked to solve his murder.

suspects.name: Numerologist Night
suspects.description: A mathematical and esoteric prodigy. Not only do they know the value of Z, they know the meaning of Z.

suspects.name: Herbalist Onyx
suspects.description: In her greenhouse, she's grown every kind of plant required in the culinary, magick, and poisoning arts.

suspects.name: High Alchemist Raven
suspects.description: There's an old joke that all alchemists are high alchemists. Raven hates it.

locations.name: The Book Ladder
locations.description: Climb up and grab a book, or just slide around the room yelling, "Wahoo!"

locations.name: The Couch
locations.description: A faux-leather place to recline at the end of the day.

locations.name: The Desk
locations.description: Topped with lots of important paperwork and a computer from the eighties.

weapons.name: A Hypnotic Pocket Watch
weapons.description: If you look deeply into this watch, you can tell the time.

weapons.name: A Deck of Marot Cards
weapons.description: You can use these murder-themed tarot cards to tell your fortune.

weapons.name: A Pseudo-Scientific Apparatus
weapons.description: It measures quantic currents to evaluate your inner blaxons.

clues: The suspect with the pseudo-scientific apparatus was born on September 7. (See Exhibit B.)
A careful search revealed a fortune-telling card wedged between two faux-leather seat cushions.

statements.statement: High Alchemist Raven was behind his desk.
Numerologist Night was on the book ladder.
Alchemically speaking, a pseudo-scientific apparatus was on the book ladder.

problem_name: The Case of the Lab with Legal Issues
problem_description: Next, the Investigation Institute sent Detective Logico to a literal mad scientist's laboratory. To clarify, the scientist wasn't crazy: he was furious. His assistant had been killed, and his research had stalled.

suspects.name: Vice President Mauve
suspects.description: A vice president of TekCo Futures. If she asks you to step into her metaverse, get out now!

suspects.name: Principal Applegreen
suspects.description: A strict principal about everything except getting away with murder. His hands are always covered in chalk.

suspects.name: Captain Slate
suspects.description: A real-life astronaut. The first woman to travel around the dark side of the moon, and also the first to be suspected of murdering her copilot.

locations.name: The Rooftop
locations.description: A giant lightning rod is connected to millions of loose wires.

locations.name: The Giant Lever
locations.description: All mad scientist lab you can flip from "OFF" to "ON."

locations.name: The Operating Table
locations.description: Leather straps could restrain a person here, or a monster.

weapons.name: A Brain in a Jar
weapons.description: The worst part is, it's oozing everywhere.

weapons.name: A Giant Magnet
weapons.description: Keep it away from any fillings. It generates a powerful electromagnetic field.

weapons.name: A Soup Ladle
weapons.description: Even a mad scientist loves soup. Particularly tomato bisque.

clues: The shortest suspect was seen hanging around beneath a sign that says "OFF."
Vice President Mauve never got near the operating table.

statements.statement: Captain Slate brought a giant magnet.
A brain in a jar was not on the rooftop.
It's as clear as the moon: Principal Applegreen brought a brain in a jar.

problem_description: On his first case with the Investigation Institute, they sent Deductive Logico to the darkest woods he'd never seen. From the shadows, he watched a witches' sabbath, thinking he was totally hidden. So he was shocked when three witches stopped the ceremony, walked over to him, and asked him to solve the murder of their sister witch.

locations.description: The money's kept in the cash register. The only thing in here is more crystals.

locations.name: The Rooftop Bar
locations.description: On top of the crystal shop is a bar where you can drink crystal-infused cocktails.

locations.name: The Outdoor Meditation Space
locations.description: A place to calmly meditate about how much money you're willing to spend here.

weapons.name: A Crystal Dagger
weapons.description: It might have some kind of ritual purpose, but it might just look great on your mantle.

weapons.name: A Deck of Marot Cards
weapons.description: You can use these murder-themed tarot cards to read your future.

weapons.name: A Crystal Ball
weapons.description: If you look into it, it will tell you your future, so long as your future is a crystal ball.

weapons.name: A Channeled Text
weapons.description: This book is longer than Gainsboro's masterpiece and was supposedly written by ghosts.

clues: The crystal dagger wanted to prove their love.
All members of the Order of the Holy Earth carried a copy of a channeled text.
Forensics determined a weapon made out of paper was present in the sage section.
Whoever would kill because the vibes were off had blue eyes.
A scrambled note recorded the movements of a suspect: PMREESU ESRMTA BLACOT WSA UDFNO DROOTOSU.
The suspect with the same height as Supreme Master Cobalt was in love with the person who brought a deck of marot cards.
Dr. Seashell, DDS, was a member of the Order of the Holy Earth.
Whoever wanted to steal a crystal was also giving off real Pisces vibes.
Whoever was in the outdoor meditation space had a heavy-weight weapon.
A Pisces was literally inside the giant safe.
Analysts discovered traces of a weapon made of crystal on the clothing of Blackstone, Esq.
The crystal salesman was killed by a crystal ball. Is that ironic?

problem_description: Logico went to a nice little diner, decorated with mementos of the town, like its hot springs and its ancient ruins and its UFO crash site. He tried to order a sandwich but was informed this was impossible, as the sandwich chef had been murdered.

suspects.name: Coach Raspberry
suspects.description: One of the best coaches this side of the Mississippi, regardless of which side you're on.

suspects.name: General Coffee
suspects.description: An espresso connoisseur who has been missing his favorite coffee cup for a long time. If he finds the person who took it, he'll kill them.

suspects.name: Chef Aubergine
suspects.description: It is said that she once killed her husband, cooked him, and then served him at her restaurant. It's not true, but just the fact that it's said about her tells you something.

suspects.name: Earl Grey
suspects.description: He comes from a long line of Earl Greys. Yes, of the tea. No, he does not give you a free bag if you ask.

locations.name: The Kitchen
locations.description: You honestly don't want to see how the food is made here.

locations.name: The Bathroom
locations.description: As much as you don't want to go into the kitchen, you really don't want to go in here.

locations.name: The Booths
locations.description: Sure, the booths are torn up and the stuffing is coming out. But it's a booth!

locations.name: The Front Patio
locations.description: The front patio has a view of the town square so you can do great people watching.

weapons.name: A Wall Knickknack
weapons.description: An old knickknack is hanging on the wall. It's some kind of old tool.

weapons.name: A Vial of Poison
weapons.description: Your typical vial of poison. Don't underestimate the classics.

weapons.name: A Spoon
weapons.description: If a fork is more gruesome than a knife, think how bad killing someone with a spoon would be.

weapons.name: Hyperallergenic Oil
weapons.description: You read that right. Everyone is deathly allergic to this.

clues: The person who wanted to liven up a party was not in the kitchen (even though cooking is a great way to liven up a party).
Whoever wanted to prove a point was right-handed.
An Aries had an old tool. That sounds like an insult, but it's just a fact.
Chef Aubergine was a member of the Order of Steel.
Someone had scrawled a scrambled clue on the plastic menu: EENNAOOY IWHT A LVIA FO NOIPOS OWDLU KILL TOU OF LEJYSUAO.
A drop of oil was discovered in the bathroom.
A Sagittarius was sitting on the front patio.
Members of the Order of Steel only carried metal weapons.
Whoever wanted to get a better seat was a Capricorn.
A spoon was used to commit the murder.

problem_description: Deductive Logico traveled to the locally famous UFO crash site. Some tourists believed it was a real crash of a real UFO. Other tourists thought it had been faked. And one tourist didn't agree with either of these positions, because he was dead.

suspects.name: Secretary Celadon
suspects.description: The secretary of defense, and someone who is personally responsible for a number of global crises, some of which are now named after her.

suspects.name: Sociologist Umber
suspects.description: As a representative from the hard sciences, she is always asking people to question their priors and if they've read Adorno.

suspects.name: Herbalist Onyx
suspects.description: In her greenhouse, she's grown every kind of plant required in the culinary, magick, and poisoning arts.

suspects.name: Dr. Seashell, DDS
suspects.description: He's an amateur physicist with a new theory of the universe, and also, he's a working dentist.

locations.name: The Crater
locations.description: At the middle is some metal equipment that looks like it might be extraterrestrial (if you squint).

locations.name: The Mouth of the Cave
locations.description: A faint light and a pulsing sound seem to come from inside.

locations.name: The Gift Shop
locations.description: You can buy a little plush alien doll, a local timeshare, or an abductee NFT.

locations.name: The Government Van
locations.description: If it is a hoax, then why is there a white government van loitering nearby?

weapons.name: A Pseudo-Scientific Apparatus
weapons.description: This one has been upgraded to measure your parquons in addition to your blaxons.

weapons.name: A Cauldron
weapons.description: If you can pick it up, you can hit someone with it. Or you can just give them a sip.

weapons.name: A Selenite Wand
weapons.description: For casting spells and bashing skulls.

weapons.name: A Hypnotic Pocket Watch
weapons.description: If you look deeply into this watch, you can tell the time.

clues: Secretary Celadon was a member of the Order of the Tar and Feather.
Whoever wanted to kill by the order of a cult was a Virgo.
A parquon-measuring device was found beside a plush doll.
Sociologist Umber had a cauldron. (In addition to being a sociologist, she was a witch.)
A scrambled message was left in the guestbook: A ELO WSA NI HET ARCERT.
Members of the Order of the Tar and Feather were not allowed to touch selenite or stand in the mouths of caves.
Whoever would kill because the vibes were off had a heavy-weight weapon.
Whoever wanted to steal the UFO was left-handed.
Either Dr. Seashell, DDS, brought a selenite wand, or he was in the mouth of the cave.
Herbalist Onyx brought a pseudo-scientific apparatus.
The tourist's body was found inside a white van.
motives: By the order of a cult

problem_description: Deductive Logico crept through the tunnels of the mysterious cave. Suddenly, he heard a scream, so he stopped creeping and started running. He didn't find a body. He found something else: some kind of underground workshop, and the secret hideout of the last three murderers. What was this place, and who was Mister Shadow, really?

suspects.name: Mister Shadow
suspects.description: A silhouette in shadow. He moves like the wind, and he looks like the night.

suspects.name: Mayor Honey
suspects.description: He knows where the bodies are buried, and he makes sure they always vote for him.

suspects.name: Blackstone, Esq.
suspects.description: Incredibly talented at the most important skill for an attorney: getting paid.

suspects.name: Dr. Seashell, DDS
suspects.description: He's an amateur physicist with a new theory of the universe, and also, he's a working dentist.

locations.name: A Big Machine
locations.description: It looks like this machine is manufacturing the so-called ancient ruins!

locations.name: The New Ruins
locations.description: Identical to the ancient ruins, except new and unruined, and with SdW stamped on the side of them.

locations.name: A Table
locations.description: The table is covered in maps of the ruin locations, plus forged historical documents.

locations.name: A Dead End
locations.description: A long tunnel that leads to a stone wall and nothing else.

weapons.name: A Giant Bone
weapons.description: What size animal could such a bone come from? And what size dog would eat it?!

weapons.name: A Giant Magnet
weapons.description: Keep it away from any fillings.

weapons.name: A Rock
weapons.description: A regular rock. But weirdly, not from this desert. And chipped.

weapons.name: A Globe
weapons.description: For plotting world domination or storing drinks.

clues: Whoever was standing by the table was right-handed.
A member of the Rite of the Flaming Earth wanted to promote the town.
The person who wanted to kill for money was not in a dead end.
Mister Shadow kept swinging his weapon, and from the sparks when it hit something, Logico could tell it was made of metal.
Whoever wanted to help win a war was giving off real Pisces vibes.
To join the Rite of the Flaming Earth, you have to be a Scorpio.
A giant bone was next to a stamp that read SdW. What does that stand for?
Either Mayor Honey brought a globe, or a globe was by a big machine.
A member of the Rite of the Flaming Earth had the globe.
A scrambled note was scrawled on the cave wall: RHVWEOE TWEADN OT LLIK FRO EYOMN LDEH A GBELO IN HEITR HDNA.
The person with the giant magnet was clearly the one responsible.
